part3.context: Listen to two people discussing the Internet. Read the opinions below and decide whose opinion matches the statements, the man, the woman, or both the man and the woman. You can listen to the discussion twice.

statements.statement: There is too much information on the Internet
Finding information on the Internet requires skills
The use of internet affects the way we think
The internet makes young people less patient

part3.explain: Woman: You know, I really feel there's too much information on the Internet. It can be overwhelming sometimes. It's hard to know what's credible. Man: Honestly, I think it's more about how we search for information. Finding what we need online requires certain skills. We need to know how to filter through all that content. Woman: Definitely! If you don't know how to search properly, you can easily get lost in all that noise. Man: And I believe the Internet affects the way we think. With so much information available, we often skim rather than think deeply about topics. Woman: That's an interesting point. I hadn't thought about that. But I do see how the constant scrolling and quick answers can make young people less patient. Man: Exactly! They expect instant results. It's like waiting for anything has become a challenge. part4.explain: Good morning, everyone! Today, I want to talk about professionalism and how it has changed over the years. To be seen as a professional, it's essential to be friendly, open-minded, and willing to help others. An optimistic attitude not only makes a good impression but also creates a better work environment. Additionally, with the rapid changes in technology and globalization, our definition of professionalism is no longer the same as it was 40 years ago. In the past, being professional often meant simply dressing well and following strict rules. Now, it includes being adaptable, understanding different cultures, and using technology effectively. As we continue to evolve in our careers, we must embrace these changes and redefine what it means to be a professional. By doing so, we can better meet the needs of our diverse workplaces and succeed in today's fast-paced world. Thank you!
